explanation: The native restart proof has one source-level false-positive path: its authentication-order check excludes only pppd-originated IPCP, not Ze-originated IPCP. Otherwise, the reviewed transport identity, injection framing, observation boundaries, latest request/Ack matching, interface-bound delivery and fresh teardown checks showed no additional actionable defect; old-daemon discrimination and rebuilt-daemon runtime confirmation remain Main's responsibility, and no validation was run.

findings.title: Reject Ze-originated IPCP before fresh authentication completes
findings.body: In l2tpPPPRestartProgress, the authentication-order guard checks only `sent [IPCP ConfReq`, which is pppd's direction. A fresh log containing Ze's `rcvd [IPCP ConfReq ...]` before the CHAP Challenge/Response, followed by successful authentication and a retransmitted request/Ack exchange, passes: l2tpPPPExchange selects the latest request and this guard ignores the earlier received packet. The retained attempt-positive-002 pppd.log confirms these direction spellings. Consequently the native proof can report authentication-before-IPCP while Ze started IPCP before authentication. RFC 1661 §3.5 requires: “Advancement from the Authentication phase to the Network-Layer Protocol phase MUST NOT occur until authentication has completed.” Reject IPCP observations in either direction before the fresh CHAP Success boundary, while retaining the post-success exchange checks.
